questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My interest in getting to learn about the culture and that there was a good study friendly environment in the city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was a lot to keep track of before leaving. It was a bit confusing in the beginning and many pages to read. However, I felt prepared by the end and before arriving. The university in Wellington also gave good information and answered quickly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I emailed a coordinator of the international student program who was very helpful in regards to student accommodation and classes.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I simply applied on their website and was offered housing closer to arrival. I can recommend applying through Victoria University of Wellington's website. It is a bit more expensive than private flatting, but I got new international friends.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived very close to my campus, which was only a 10 minute walk. However, Wellington is extremely walkable.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A bit expensive, though.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Long

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: A lot of communication back and forward, but people were really nice.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could text them. Otherwise, the website had a lot of information.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful. It was not hard at all, and there are many options.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take the courses that interest you. You DO have to study while being here - it is not only fun.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two 100 level courses and a 200 level course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is more in-person classes than at UCPH, and you have to write more assignments throughout the trimester. The exam periods are less intense.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I took Intercultural Communication, Anthropology, and Māori Culture and Society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Māori Culture and Society was amazing. It is a hard class for foreigners as they use Te Reo Māori to describe concepts and parts of the culture, but it gives you a unique insight on this incredible indigenous culture. Our teacher Brian was so nice and we had many guest lecturers.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: If your own insurance does not cover going to the hospital, the university requires you to buy their own.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee is way cheaper than in Denmark, and so is it eating out. Alcohol is way more expensive. Groceries are also generally more expensive. However, the farmers market on Sundays have affordable vegetables and fruits.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I joined the Recreation Center which was a really good investment. I also joined the tramping club which offered and planed hikes and bouldering. They also had many clubs and activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the Recreation Center as you can work out on your own or take group fitness classes. It is a good way to clear your mind and meet new people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Going to the CBD is always really nice. There are plenty of treks in the area that are worth exploring. In the mid-tri break we went on a roadtrip on the North Island, which was really cool.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was really easy. I found that I could basically keep my routine and that people are really nice.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Student housing will help and joining a club. Definitely participate in the Orientation Week before classes start.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Dating...

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are really friendly and helpful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Make sure to plan a good schedule so that you have room to write your assignments
2. They do not have power sockets for you to charge your computers in the lecture halls, so charge your computer from home
3. You are in a country where many different cultures and ethnicities meet - be respectful and open to seeing them expressed in your everyday life

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are three different campus'. Kelburn is really cool and where I had all my classes. Te Aro is in the CBD, and Pipitea is closer to the stadium.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I have gotten a unique insight to a different culture consisting of many cultures, which I have enjoyed immensely.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing learning about an indigenous culture and understanding the responsibility I have to support them.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
